summary: Created an SSH host certificate authority on node1 and configured sshd to present a CA-signed host certificate, so clients trusting only the CA (no host-key pinning) connect cleanly. Verified before and after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: openssh-server installed, ssh.socket active but no host keys existed yet
Created dedicated CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca (ed25519, root-only private key)
Signed the ed25519 host public key with the CA (ssh-keygen -s), producing /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1, 10.100.214.10, localhost, 52-week validity
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf with HostCertificate directive; validated config with sshd -t (after fixing missing /run/sshd)
Restarted ssh service to load the certificate

Verified with an SSH client trusting only the CA public key via @cert-authority in known_hosts and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes (no host key pinned) — connection accepted the cert, failing only later on publickey auth
Captured baseline boot_id and service state on node1
Scheduled and executed a native reboot (systemd-run + systemctl reboot) with the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again; confirmed changed boot_id proving an actual restart
Re-verified ssh.socket active, certificate files intact, and CA-trust-based client verification still succeeds post-reboot

evidence.summary: Generated /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca ed25519 CA keypair with root-only permissions

evidence.requirement: Host certificate signed by the CA and installed
evidence.summary: Signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub with the CA producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub, configured HostCertificate in sshd_config.d, validated config, restarted ssh, confirmed listening on :22

evidence.requirement: Client trusts CA (not pinned host key) and connects without pinning
evidence.summary: known_hosts contained only an @cert-authority line (no pinned host key); ssh with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes reported 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate', failing only later on publickey auth
Captured boot_id bfd05127-... and confirmed ssh.socket/ssh active plus cert files present before reboot
systemd-run scheduled systemctl reboot and returned 'REBOOT_SCHEDULED' acknowledgement immediately

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Connection dropped mid-command during reboot, then reconnection showed new boot_id 56c34e23-... differing from baseline bfd05127-...

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and cert data
evidence.summary: ssh.socket active and listening on :22, CA and host-cert files intact, and CA-trust-only client verification again succeeded post-reboot
